story_title: As the system, I want to detect overlapping venue bookings so that a venue cannot be double-booked for incompatible events

acceptance_criteria.text: The system checks existing bookings when a venue booking is requested.

Conflict checking is performed per fixed slot (AM, PM, Night); two bookings in different slots on the same day for the same venue do not conflict unless one's setup or turnaround requirement occupies the other's slot.
An overlapping confirmed booking is detected.
An overlapping pending booking request is detected: only one active pending request or confirmed booking may exist for the same venue and slot.
A booking request cannot be submitted if it conflicts with an existing pending request or confirmed booking.
A booking request cannot be confirmed if it conflicts with an existing confirmed booking.
A rejected, withdrawn or released booking does not count as a conflict.
Venue unavailability is treated as a conflict.
The conflicting booking or unavailable period is identified to the authorised user.

test_cases.title: A confirmed booking cannot be approved over another confirmed booking
test_cases.preconditions: BLOCKED — there is no way to confirm a booking in the application. Venue Staff's 'Booking Requests' screen lists pending requests but has no Approve or Reject action; that belongs to Venue Booking Approval (SPM-43), which has no endpoint and no branch. The rule itself is implemented and unit tested in src/lib/venueConflict.ts (checkVenueBookingApproval, scope 'approved') — see open question 1.
steps: Log in as Venue Staff Marcus Wong (marcus.wong@connectsphere.com / password123)

When SPM-43 builds it, approving must be refused with the conflicting booking named, and the unit tests in src/lib/__tests__/venueConflict.test.ts already pin that behaviour.

open_questions: AC6 cannot be tested through the application: nothing can confirm a booking. Venue Staff's Booking Requests screen is read-only and bookings/page.tsx says in a comment that Approve and Reject belong to Venue Booking Approval (SPM-43), which has no endpoint and no branch. SPM-44 implements and unit tests the rule (checkVenueBookingApproval in src/lib/venueConflict.ts, 5 tests), including the part that differs from request time: at confirm time a rival PENDING request must NOT block, because approving one request is exactly how Venue Staff choose between two. Whoever builds SPM-43 should call that function rather than write the rule again. Confirm this split is what you want.

AC4 says 'only one active pending request or confirmed booking may exist for the same venue and slot'. The system enforces this at request time, so a second pending request can never be created through the application. It does NOT retroactively police rows that already exist: if two pending requests somehow end up in the database for one slot, nothing flags them. Is enforcement at the point of writing sufficient, or should the system also report existing duplicates?

SPM-44 made the refusal messages more specific (AC9), which changed the wording SPM-42's recorded test cases assert. SPM-42-TC14 and SPM-42-TC15 in docs/test-cases/SPM-42_Test_Cases.xlsx still expect 'Marina Auditorium is already booked for this time.' and will now read '… is already booked for EVT-… Product Showcase on 21 Oct 2026, AM–PM.' The unit tests have been updated; the SPM-42 workbook has not, because changing another story's recorded expectations is the author's call. Decide whether to update those two expected results or re-run SPM-42 and record the new wording.

RESOLVED 2026-10-02: AC2's first half (different slots do not conflict) is only observable at a venue with no setup or turnaround time — at every seeded venue the preparation slot makes neighbouring slots clash. SPM-44's fixture script therefore creates its own room, SPM44 Conflict Room (SPM44-PLN, setup 0, teardown 0), rather than reusing SPM-42's SPM42 Plain Room.

Raised while validating SPM-44-TC01. A venue whose slot is already taken is still shown as 'Suitable' with a 'Request booking' button on the event's Venue tab; the conflict is only reported when the request is submitted. That is consistent with SPM-41, where suitability means capacity, layout and facilities rather than occupancy, and the search screen (SPM-44-TC09) does drop the room once a time window is given. It still means a coordinator can open the booking screen for a room they cannot have. Should the Venue tab mark an occupied room, or is finding out on submit acceptable?
